tensions.poleA: A building open to the street
tensions.narrative: The ground-floor debate was the day's sharpest split. One group sees openness as the point of the place. Another pays for calm and heard the proposal as selling the one thing they cannot get anywhere else.
tensions.toResolve: Whether openness and quiet can be separated by floor and time, or whether one has to win.

tensions.narrative: The programme team protects quality and coherence. Members describe their best experiences as unprogrammed and want permission more than production. Both sides cite the accidental compost debate as proof.
tensions.toResolve: What the programme team's job becomes if members host: gatekeeper, coach, or infrastructure.

tensions.narrative: The governance conversation kept returning to the same admission: consensus has become a way to postpone. Small choices get voted on, big ones wait, and the board and membership meet too rarely to close the gap.
tensions.toResolve: Which decisions the group is willing to delegate, and to whom, before the next budget cycle.
